card: PR #36109 extracts arbitrary-parent block template reconstruction into a shared SwitchBlockParent test helper used by BuildChain and MinerTestingSetup::Block. It recalculates the proof-of-work target and coinbase subsidy from the target parent, pads coinbase scriptSigs with OP_0 to satisfy minimum length requirements on heights 1-16, and enforces coinbase-only templates to avoid discarding transaction fees. This fixes bad-cb-amount and bad-cb-length validation errors when test utilities generate forks across halvings or near genesis.
changed_since_previous: Renamed the extracted helper from RebuildBlockForParent to SwitchBlockParent, explicitly passed use_mempool = false in MinerTestingSetup::Block, and added unit tests exercising SwitchBlockParent's target and coinbase calculations.
evidence: PR description notes that 'Existing reorg tests can underpay without failing, while a fork crossing a halving can overpay and fail with bad-cb-amount' and 'Coinbase input scripts containing only the height also fail with bad-cb-length at heights 1 through 16'
Commit 9fdac77721 demonstrates the failure by characterizing a fork from genesis through the first halving
problem: Test helpers that attach active-tip templates to arbitrary parent blocks retained the active tip's subsidy and target. As a result, building forks across halving boundaries could overpay and fail with bad-cb-amount, and coinbase scripts at heights 1 through 16 lacked padding and failed with bad-cb-length.

risk.why: A mistake would only cause unit test failures or produce invalid test blocks without affecting production code.

summary: Unifies parent-dependent block template reconstruction into a shared SwitchBlockParent test helper used by BuildChain and MinerTestingSetup::Block. The helper updates hashPrevBlock, timestamp, and merkle root while recalculating nBits and the coinbase subsidy from the actual parent. It also pads coinbase scriptSigs with OP_0 to meet BIP 34 minimum length requirements on low heights and asserts that templates are coinbase-only.
